page: Microsoft Azure D96ls_v7 is a compute-focused instance within the Dlsv7 family, configured with 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V, the system features dedicated core allocations backed by a large 480 MB L3 cache. It incorporates 192.0 GB of memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. No local physical storage or GPUs are included, requiring external Premium Storage for non-volatile disk persistence.

Performance benchmarks reflect substantial parallel processing capacity and advanced vector capabilities. The processor supports AVX-512 and Intel AMX instruction sets, contributing to top-tier benchmark results in PassMark CPU tests (104,787.21) and extended instruction evaluations. Multi-threaded decompression reaches 575.95 GB/s, while Clang compilation benchmarks register 58,511.0, both placing in the upper ten percent. In-memory data structures perform effectively, demonstrated by Redis SET operations processing 151.03 million operations per second and static web throughput measuring 142.01 GB/s.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the D96ls_v7 is tailored for CPU-bound applications that do not require high memory footprints per thread. This resource distribution delivers cost efficiency by minimizing expenditure on unneeded RAM while sustaining high compute density. Tradeoffs include the lack of bundled local NVMe storage and limited memory per core for heavy caching datasets. Recommended workloads encompass large-scale software compilation, distributed compute tasks, CI/CD runners, network-level web traffic handling, and quantized integer-based machine learning inference.
description: Microsoft Azure D96ls_v7 is a compute-dense virtual machine within the Dlsv7 series, featuring 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. Supported by 192.0 GB of RAM, a 480 MB L3 cache, and instruction sets including AVX-512 and AMX, the server exhibits strong throughput in compute and vector-heavy execution. Benchmark outcomes confirm top-tier performance in PassMark CPU ratings, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, software build tasks via Clang, and Redis key-value workloads. The instance bundles no local disk storage or graphical accelerators, relying on remote network volumes for persistent storage. Given its 1:2 memory-to-core configuration, the D96ls_v7 avoids the cost overhead of high memory capacity, making it a viable architecture for parallel batch processing, continuous integration build clusters, static web serving infrastructure, and CPU-driven mathematical modeling.
